sentences: Pivot-minors use edge-pivot operations together with vertex deletion to simplify graphs.
The source asks whether sufficiently large rank-width forces every fixed bipartite circle graph as such a minor.
The conclusion would supply a universal family of structural obstructions witnessing high cut-rank complexity.
This parallels excluded-grid principles while using graph transformations tailored to rank-width.

The threshold may depend on the fixed target graph, and the source's pivot and circle-graph conventions must be recovered before the statement is compared with ordinary graph-minor or vertex-minor theorems.
